test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 29 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statement.

**Statements:**

Few mice are rats

Most rats are vultures

All vultures are hawks

**Conclusions:**

(I) Few mice are vultures

(II) Some hawks are mice

(III) Some rats are hawks

options.text: All conclusions I, II and III follow
Only conclusion I and III follow

solution:
Statements:

Few mice are rats

Most rats are vultures

All vultures are hawks

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/117e4ff563b5ed0e7ab7b99f56de8189e945a9eb0351553ebeff0c48eba00950.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Few mice are vultures → False (There is no direct relationship between mice and vultures, so it can be possible not definite).

(II) Some hawks are mice → False (There is no direct relationship between mice and hawks, so it can be possible not definite).

(III) Some rats are hawks →** True** (As most rats are vultures and all vultures are hawks, some rats are also hawks).

So,** 'Only conclusion III follows '.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__**

**1) “ALL” can be written as: Each, Every, Only, 100%.**

**2) “Some” and “Some not” can be written as: Almost, Little, Few, At most, At least, Many, Mostly, 1-99%.**

**3) “No” can be written as: None, 0%.**
